classification.habitat: Dry deciduous and subtropical habitats; commonly found on hills and forest margins
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in the Indian subcontinent

identification.description: Much-branched shrub recognized by small leaves and numerous reddish flowers borne along the branches.
identification.whole_plant: Erect, much-branched shrub with numerous slender branches.
identification.root: Woody root system; root is not the characteristic identifying organ of the crude flower drug.
identification.stem: Woody, branched stems; older portions become brownish.
identification.leaf: Small, simple, opposite to subopposite leaves, elliptic to lanceolate with entire margin.
identification.flower: Small, showy reddish to orange-red flowers borne in clusters along the branches; the flowers are the characteristic medicinal part.
identification.fruit: Small dry capsule developing after flowering.
identification.bark: Thin bark on young branches; not the principal crude drug in this dossier.
identification_points: Flowers used as the characteristic crude drug

therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated flowers and an authoritative formulation/reference for therapeutic dosing.
therapeutics.contraindications: No project-specific contraindication claim added without text-level verification.

major_constituents: Tannins and other phenolic constituents are reported from the flowers
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Constituent profiles vary by plant material and analytical method; no assay value is asserted here.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Woodfordia fruticosa is an important Ayurvedic medicinal shrub; its flowers are also traditionally used in fermentation processes. This dossier does not treat traditional use as proof of clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authenticate the plant and crude drug before use. Therapeutic dosing should be taken from an authoritative formulation or pharmacopoeial source.

exam_points: Characteristic: numerous reddish flowers on branches
viva_questions: What is the botanical name of Dhataki?
Which family does Dhataki belong to?
What is the characteristic flower colour?
student.quick_revision: Dhataki is Woodfordia fruticosa, a branched Lythraceae shrub whose flowers are the characteristic medicinal part.

teaching_points: Demonstrate the shrub habit and branch-associated flower clusters.
Explain why crude-drug identification should include flower morphology.
discussion_points: Traditional role of Dhataki in fermented preparations
Difference between botanical identity and crude-drug identity
practical_points: Examine authenticated dried flowers under magnification.
Record colour, size, odour and attached floral structures.
Compare genuine material with an unidentified market sample only under supervision.

doctor.quick_reference: Dhataki — Woodfordia fruticosa (L.) Kurz; Lythraceae; principal drug part: flower. Indexed traditional indications include Atisara, Pravahika, Pradara, Trishna and Vrana.
key_precautions: Use authoritative formulation-specific dosing rather than this educational record.
Do not equate traditional indication with established modern clinical efficacy.
